result.content: {"answer_sections": [{"text": "The source states that Astypalaia provided safe anchorages for corsairs, offering provisions and water.", "claim_ids": ["c-4c1222f0df72fb1ae71a"]}, {"text": "Corsairs lurked in Oran, Tlemcen, Tenes, Shershell, Bougie, Jigelli, Bizerta, Sfax, Susa, Monastir, Jerbah, and Tripoli, ready for raids.", "claim_ids": ["c-e5bbc3264384075aa4f5"]}, {"text": "The source mentions that Dutch and English privateers found refuge in North Africa, authorized to continue their war under new banners.", "claim_ids": ["c-bfc89e03ec488328ba0a"]}, {"text": "In 1624, Tunisian leadership explained to Ottoman and Venetian envoys that corsairs had no choice but to attack the Venetian Ionian islands.", "claim_ids": ["c-5aa00ba29f4eb196d20e"]}], "unknowns": ["The exact locations and dates of some anchorages and raid locations are not specified in the sources.", "The specific activities of Ottoman limans in the Mediterranean during the second half of the 17th century are not fully detailed."], "limitations": ["Some sources are secondary and require further criticism.", "The classification status of some claims is provisional, indicating the need for source analysis."]}
